card.title: Metals, Insulators and Semiconductors – Band Theory

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Band theory sorts solids into three classes. **Metals** (Cu, Ag): overlapping or partly-filled bands — abundant free electrons, ρ ~ 10⁻⁸ Ω·m. **Insulators** (diamond, E_g ≈ 6 eV): full valence band, empty conduction band, gap > 3 eV — no carriers, ρ up to 10²⁰ Ω·m.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - ρ_metal ~ 10⁻⁸ Ω·m; ρ_semiconductor ~ 10⁻⁵–10² Ω·m; ρ_insulator ~ 10¹²–10²⁰ Ω·m - E_g: Si 1.1 eV, Ge 0.7 eV, diamond ~6 eV

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Semiconductors are insulators at 0 K** — all their carriers come from thermal excitation or doping.  ·  **A full band cannot conduct** — no empty states to move into.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Reasoning (2m): Why does a pure semiconductor conduct better at 50 °C than at 0 °C?** — Higher temperature breaks more covalent bonds, creating more electron–hole pairs; carrier density rises, so conductivity rises (opposite to metals).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Opposite temperature signatures** — semiconductor conductivity rises with T, metal's falls.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Metals: overlap/partly filled. Insulators: E_g > 3 eV. Semiconductors: ~1 eV, pairs at room T.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Resistivity spans ~10⁻⁸ to 10²⁰ Ω·m across the three classes — 28 orders of magnitude.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Three Classes, One Diagram Whether a material conducts copper-like, blocks diamond-like or sits between like silicon is decided entirely by its band picture: overlap, wide gap or narrow gap. This topic turns that classification into a comparison table you can reproduce under exam pressure.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 The three classes by band structure - **Metals (conductors):** valence and conduction bands overlap, or the conduction band is partially filled. Electrons find empty states immediately above and drift freely under tiny fields. Examples: Cu, Ag, Al. Resistivity ~10⁻⁸ Ω·m.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 112:** this is the classification that the band picture makes possible. - **To Topic 114:** semiconductors' usefulness comes from controlling their carrier population. - **To resistance (Topic 99):** resistivity spans ~28 orders of magnitude across the classes.
